title: Q3 town hall
transcript:
Linda Brandt: Good afternoon everyone, let's get started. Thanks for joining the Q3 town hall. Agenda today: one, department updates from Trading, Wealth, Lending, Risk and Operations. Two, the KYCPipeline ownership transfer. Three, the legacy reconciliation plan. Four, open questions and action items. Wendy is taking notes and will circulate them Monday.
Wendy Dyer: Confirmed. I'll post the notes and action list in #general by end of day Monday, and I'll put follow-up dates on the calendar.
Linda Brandt: Great. Daniel, let's start with Trading.
Daniel Reyes: Thanks, Linda. Volumes in the quarter have been solid, with the desk seeing higher flow in the last six weeks. The main thing I want to flag is OMS stability. We had two slow-login episodes tied to AuthSSO, and the desk lost a few minutes each time. Technology has a fix in testing. Second, we are adding two more quant strategies to the pre-trade checks, and Risk needs to sign off before we go live.
Owen Gallagher: Happy to do that, Daniel. We just need the parameter documentation at least a week ahead so we can run it through RiskEngine against the current limits.
Daniel Reyes: Understood. I'll have the documentation to you by Friday July 31.
Owen Gallagher: Perfect. Let me give the Risk update while I have the floor. Intraday VaR runs are completing on time, and the RiskEngine latency work we flagged last quarter is done. We've still seen occasional delays when PricingSvc is slow in the morning, since RiskEngine depends on it. We are tightening the alerting so we catch that before the desk does. We're also reviewing our concentration limits for the lending book, and I'd like to review that with Brian.
Brian Kowalski: Yes, please. On the Lending side, the pipeline is healthy. Origination volumes are up for the quarter, and turnaround on underwriting is down by roughly a day. The constraint right now is LoanOrigination, which depends on KYCPipeline. When KYC slows down, our closings slow down. So the ownership change matters a lot to us.
Linda Brandt: Good segue. Ravi, can you cover the KYCPipeline transfer?
Ravi Patel: Sure. As announced, KYCPipeline moves from Operations to Compliance on October 6. Until then Operations owns it, and we remain accountable for incidents. The plan is a runbook handover, an on-call rotation transition, and a joint review of the open backlog. We'll finish the runbook by end of August, then do two shadow weeks in September with the Compliance team. One risk: the pipeline depends on ClientHub, DocVault and SanctionsScreen, so the handover needs to cover those integrations as well.
Grace Lin: From the Wealth side, onboarding is the biggest pain point, so we're keen on this. Our advisors want a clear escalation path when a case gets stuck. Can we get a single contact during the transition?
Ravi Patel: Yes. I'll name an interim contact in Operations, and we'll agree on a Compliance contact before October 6. I'll send that out by August 7.
Grace Lin: Thank you. A quick update on Wealth. Assets under advisement are up on the quarter, mostly on market performance. PortfolioMgr rebalancing runs had a couple of delays when pricing data lagged. The team is also piloting a new client review template that cuts prep time. We'll decide on a full rollout at the end of August.
Linda Brandt: Thanks, Grace. Ravi, what about the reconciliation plan?
Ravi Patel: ReconLegacy is our end-of-day batch, written in Perl on Oracle 11g. It still depends on SettlementEngine and GLCore, and every break there lands on my team. The decision from the steering group is to start a replacement project in Q4, with parallel runs before we retire the legacy batch. Technology is scoping it. For now, the immediate action is to document the current break categories, so nothing is lost in migration. My team will have that written by August 21.
Owen Gallagher: Risk would like to be in the design review, since ReportingBI pulls from GLCore and we don't want surprises in the regulatory reports.
Ravi Patel: Agreed. I'll include you and your team in the scoping session.
Linda Brandt: Let me record the decisions. One, the KYCPipeline transfer date stays October 6. Two, the ReconLegacy replacement kicks off in Q4, with Risk in the design review. Three, the new quant checks need Risk sign-off before go-live. Any objections?
Daniel Reyes: None from Trading, as long as the sign-off doesn't slip past mid-August.
Owen Gallagher: We can turn it around within two weeks of receiving the documentation.
Linda Brandt: Good. Now questions. Anything from the floor?
Brian Kowalski: One more thing. Can we get a view of KYC turnaround times by week during the transition, so Lending can plan closings?
Ravi Patel: I can produce a weekly turnaround summary starting in August. I'll share it in #kyc-pipeline.
Linda Brandt: Perfect. Let me summarize the action items. Daniel sends the quant check documentation to Risk by July 31. Ravi names the interim contact by August 7, documents the recon break categories by August 21, and posts the weekly KYC turnaround summary starting in August. Owen tightens the PricingSvc delay alerting and schedules the Lending concentration review with Brian. Grace decides on the client review template rollout at the end of August. Wendy circulates the notes Monday. Thanks everyone, we'll close here.
Wendy Dyer: Notes will be out Monday. Thanks, all.
